newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria stocks index slips further in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria stocks index slips further in slack trade.

text.p: Nigeria's all-share index, which measures the performance of the local stock market, dropped sharply on Thursday for the second day running as declining demand for shares took its toll, dealers said.
The index closed at 8688.83 from 8713.99 on Wednesday. It was 8716.59 on Tuesday.
"There are still many shares on offer but not many investors," said one broker.
Worst hit was oil stock Agip, which dropped by 90 kobo to 23.00 naira after falling by 10 kobo on Wednesday.
"There is a chunk of Agip shares around," said the broker.
Guinness dropped 80 kobo to 7.90 on dividend payment following its announcement on Tuesday of an improved full year profit for 1996.

Conglomerate UAC fell 20 kobo to 18.40 naira while leading banks First Bank and Afribank lost 10 kobo apiece to 15.20 naira and 6.90 naira respectively. First Bank fell by the same margin on Wednesday.
Unipetrol extended its recent losses by 10 kobo to close at 70.40 naira. It fell by 50 kobo on Wednesday.

Among the few gainers was food and beverages powerhouse Nestle Foods Plc, which continues to defy the bearish trend in the market by adding one naira on Thursday to 83.00 naira after rising by 80 kobo on Wednesday.
Nestle became the highest priced stock on the Nigerian bourse last week when it announced a doubling of its 1996 full year profit and a generous dividend.
"Nestle is the only stock on the exchange that is still being actively sought for in these lean times," said one trader.
BOC gases, formerly Industrial Gases Plc, which rose by 30 kobo on Wednesday gained another 10 kobo on Thursday to 13.60 naira.
